tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...') and lists explicit trigger scenarios phrased in terms of what the user is experiencing (slow application, alarm firing, timeouts, idle-call slowness, flat dashboard, pre-peak review, comparing latency across operations), which is user-intent focused rather than implementation-focused. It also summarizes the skill's output (six outcomes, confidence, signals, handoff) concisely in a single paragraph. It covers triggers even when the user doesn't explicitly say 'DynamoDB latency diagnosis' (e.g. 'application is slow', 'latency dashboard looks flat while users still see slow writes').
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when someone asks whether Amazon DynamoDB is why their application is slow — a table shows high or spiky p99 or average latency, a SuccessfulRequestLatency alarm fired, requests intermittently time out, the first call after idle is slow, or the latency dashboard looks flat while users still see slow writes."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays focused on domain-specific procedures (metric semantics, outcome classification, scope boundaries) and does not explain general concepts like what CloudWatch or DynamoDB are. Every sentence conveys non-obvious, skill-specific information.
tests.evidence: 'SuccessfulRequestLatency measures time internal to the DynamoDB service — client activity and network trip times are excluded — and only for successful requests, so throttled and failed calls never appear in it.'

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (exact queries, thresholds, templates) is explicitly deferred to references/ files; the body only contains summaries, outcome names, and high-level rules, even within conditional branches like the outcomes table.
tests.evidence: 'load after collection, before classifying.** Reference values, elevation tests, patterns, the selection order, confidence, contributing factors, and verbatim templates.'

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All four reference files are linked with markdown link syntax in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with an explicit trigger describing when to load it.
tests.evidence: 'load before the first API call.' ... 'load after collection, before classifying.' ... 'load before writing the report.' ... 'load before explaining how any metric... behaves'

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (read-only allowlist, classification order, validation before output) are given exact prescriptive rules, while flexible areas (which measurement to use when DynamoDB isn't the cause, how to present hypotheses) are described with purpose and freedom.
tests.evidence: 'READ ONLY. Only the operations in the data-collection allowlist... this skill never reads item data.' vs 'Say "not explained by DynamoDB-side metrics", list the candidate places the time could be as unconfirmed, and name the measurement that would find it'

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where it hands off to other capabilities, the skill designates a clear default path (its own analysis) and names specific alternative skills/tools as escape hatches rather than listing many equal options.
tests.evidence: 'DNS failures, VPC endpoint or connectivity errors | The aws-vpc-dns-investigation skill' and 'name the measurement that would find it: SDK latency metric logging, application tracing, or the aws-vpc-dns-investigation skill.'

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (parse input, collect, classify, validate) applicable to any table/operation, not a one-off instance; specific details like outcome codes and templates support but don't replace the generalization.
tests.evidence: '1. Parse and validate input... 2. Collect... 5. Classify... 8. Validate before output' — a reusable workflow for any table/operation combination.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive section of non-obvious domain pitfalls that correct likely agent mistakes, functioning as a gotchas section.
tests.evidence: 'A clean SuccessfulRequestLatency rules out DynamoDB processing time — nothing more.' and 'A flat curve beside throttle events is consistent with retry-inflated client latency... it does not rule throttling out.'

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly defers the report structure/template to a dedicated reference file rather than omitting it.
tests.evidence: '[references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) — load before writing the report. Structure, recommended-action preconditions, health rating, and the pre-render validation checks.'
